title.narrative: Upscaling Education, Protection and WASH services for vulnerable children and their caregivers in Akkar

description.narrative: ltpgtDue to the Syrian war, economic deterioration and political deadlock, Lebanon suffers from a severe humanitarian crisis. This has inflicted catastrophic economic and social consequences, intensifying poverty and worsening development. Vulnerable populations, particularly children and adolescents living in poverty, endure cumulative deprivations such as being out of school, are subjected to violence both in schools and in their homes, engaged in child labor affecting about 100,000 children (4 to 6%, depending on nationality), or forced into child marriage. The crisis also undermines parents' ability to care for and safeguard children. They thus resort to negative coping mechanisms, restricting access to education, pushing girls into early marriages, and subjecting children to labor and begging. The long-term consequences on children will persist throughout their lives. Educating and protecting children and adolescents requires an effective intervention based on the priorities set by the relevant sectors.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtRMF has designed a 12-month multi-sectoral humanitarian project to enhance the well-being and resilience of children in 12 identified localities in Akkar. The project localities include Abdel, Al Hakour, Bebnine, Halba, Hosniyeh, Mhammara, Minyara, Ouadi Al Jamous, Qleiaa, Qobbet Chamra, and Sammounieh, Semmaquiye. ltspangtTlt/spangtltspangthese localities were identified through coordination with MAKANI partners, to complement efforts and prevent overlap. This intervention constitutes a holistic approach in which 950 children will each be engaged in all the project’s Education, Protection, and WASH activities.
